edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 5

source_text: Trahe me post te; curremus in odorem unguentorum tuorum. Sponsa se trahi petit, quia sine Verbi tractu currere non potest. Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua: secreta sapientiae et mysteria Scripturarum. Exsultemus et laetemur in te: non in nobis, sed in sponso. Memores uberum tuorum super vinum: recte diligunt te.
pass_a_gloss: Draw me after you; we-will-run into fragrance of-ointments your. Bride herself to-be-drawn asks, because without of-Word drawing to-run she-is-not-able. He-brought-in me king into chambers his: secrets of-wisdom and mysteries of-Scriptures...
pass_b_english: [[Draw me after you; we will run into the fragrance of your ointments >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]. The Bride asks to be drawn, because without the Word’s drawing she cannot run. [[The king has brought me into his chambers >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]: the secrets of wisdom and the mysteries of the Scriptures. Let us exult and rejoice in you: not in ourselves, but in the Bridegroom. Mindful of your breasts above wine: rightly do they love you.
